title: cost-model-led-dynamic-batcher
author: Priya Malhotra
description: Motivation: mixed-sequence-length workloads waste GPU cycles due to padding and miss opportunities for KV cache reuse. This PR introduces a lightweight runtime cost model and a greedy merging heuristic that trades off padding overhead, kernel-fit efficiency, and KV cache affinity when composing dynamic inference batches. Design summary: 1) cost_model module: per-model kernel profiles (warmup cost, per-token cost, preferred tile sizes) and a compact online estimator that tracks recent sequence-length histogram and prefix-correlation scores. 2) greedy-cost-merger: when the batcher receives a small backlog it scores candidate merges using cost = alpha*expected_padding_tokens*token_cost + beta*kernel_mismatch_penalty + gamma*(1 - kv_affinity_score)*kv_warm_cost, where coefficients are tunable via dynamic_batcher.cost_alpha,beta,gamma. The merger prefers grouping sequences with high KV affinity (shared recent prefixes) even if they differ slightly in length, to exploit KV cache hits for multi-step decoding. 3) kernel hint propagation: the batcher annotates assembled batches with a kernel_hint to help the scheduler pick precompiled kernels that maximize throughput for the effective sequence-length distribution. 4) metrics & tracing: added dynamic_batcher.{chosen_strategy,predicted_padding,kv_affinity,kernel_hint} metrics and tracing points for end-to-end correlation. Backwards compatibility: default coefficients match the existing behavior (pure length bucketing) so rollout is conservative. Config: new runtime config section dynamic_batcher.cost_model_profile (per-model override) and an operator flag dynamic_batcher.enable_cost_merging. Implementation highlights: - src/runtime/cost_model.rs implements compact kernel profiles and an exponentially weighted histogram for sequence lengths. - src/runtime/dynamic_batcher.rs implements the greedy-cost-merger as a pluggable strategy alongside existing bucketing strategies. - src/runtime/kv_affinity.rs computes a fast fingerprint over recent prefixes to estimate KV reuse probability without materializing KV state. - scheduler accepts kernel_hint in schedule decision to prioritize kernels optimized for expected output length/beam size. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on mixed workloads (50% short (<=32), 30% medium (128-256), 20% long (1024+)) across r5 gpus and a Llama-variant model show: - 9.8% median throughput improvement (tokens/s) vs current seqlen-bucketing baseline - 14.6% reduction in padding tokens processed per request - 11.2% lower inferred GPU cost per 1M tokens in our cost estimator - Tail latency (p95) unchanged within noise for these configs Rollout plan: start as opt-in config for Canary workspace, collect the new metrics for 48h, then enable for small production tenants with automatic rollback if predicted_padding increases by >5% or if p99 latency regresses by >10%. Checklist: [x] unit tests for cost evaluation and merger decisions [x] e2e benchmark manifests [x] metrics and tracing hooks [x] docs update describing new config flags [x] feature gated behind dynamic_batcher.enable_cost_merging Changes include small illustrative code updates, tests, configs and docs. See files_changed list for specifics.

review_comments: Jared Cohen: Nit - please add a short doc snippet explaining how coeffs alpha/beta/gamma interact with autoscaling. Also, can we add a safety check so cost model state doesn't grow unbounded for very high cardinality seqlen streams?
Priya Malhotra: replied - added doc snippet and bounded histogram with EWMA forgetting factor; updated tests to assert memory bound under synthetic high-cardinality workload.
Lena Ortiz: Requested changes - include a regression test for the case where KV affinity scoring is noisy (false positives) to ensure we don't regress tail latency.
Priya Malhotra: replied - added a randomized noise test and a conservative backoff in the merger when affinity confidence < 0.6. Also added tracing to surface affinity confidence in dashboards.
release_notes: Introduce a cost-model-driven dynamic batcher that reduces padding and exploits KV cache affinity for mixed-length workloads. Opt-in via dynamic_batcher.enable_cost_merging; exposes new metrics for tuning. Expected throughput gains for heterogeneous workloads; rollout guarded by canary and automatic rollback thresholds.
